守礼.name: Shurei
守礼.desc: A long-established diner in Isagawa, Nago. Its old-fashioned tiled roof has a lot of character. A gentle bonito-based soup with flat noodles, topped with braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), rolled omelet, and fried tofu, for an outstanding value of ¥500. It also serves Nago's specialty, hitō (dolphin) dishes.
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map," and I ate here in March 2021 😄
Shokudo Shurei (the old-style tiled roof has a lot of character lol)
In the "Nago Soba Map," "Shurei" is featured as shop 41 of 41
I ordered the "Soba" that was introduced in the map.
Soba　¥500
A gentle bonito-based soup with flat noodles. The toppings are plentiful too—braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), rolled omelet, and fried tofu—yet it's ¥500 😁　More reasonable than other shops.

Rating (9/15): Solidly tasty and reasonable. The set meals apparently come with free rice refills, which is also good value 😁　Nago is famous for hitō (dolphin), and it was on the menu. Next time I'd like to try a dolphin dish too.

守良屋（すろーやー）.name: Suroya
守良屋（すろーやー）.desc: A popular handmade Okinawa soba shop tucked away deep in the Kyoda village. Committed to using no chemical seasonings, with glossy homemade wavy flat noodles and a light, gentle bonito broth. A natural style with windows wide open and only electric fans.
t: Driving along National Route 58 in Kyoda, Nago, I'd been curious about a handmade sign reading "Handmade Okinawa Soba Suroya," and I finally went to eat here in July 2023 😊
The turnoff from National Route 58 in Kyoda, Nago, to "Suroya"
A handmade sign with character 😄
Going deep along the narrow village road, "Suroya" was at the dead end 😁
There was no menu; the soba menu was posted on the wall of the building.
Since you access it from the national highway via a narrow road through the village, it's a quiet, tucked-away place, but inside it was packed with locals and tourists (・・)
As usual, I went in without any research, but I think it's a popular shop.

I ordered the "Suroya Soba," which has the same name as the shop. Because I hadn't done any research, I didn't know how to read the kanji, and when ordering I ended up saying "Moriyoshi-ya soba, please," but my order went through just fine (^_^;)　When I googled it after eating, I learned it's read "Suroya" (^_^;)
"Suroya Soba" ¥950
On the wall inside was a notice saying "No chemical seasonings used." I got the impression they're quite particular about making things with natural ingredients.

First, a sip of the soup. A gentle flavor with a light bonito broth coming through; solidly tasty 😋　The noodles are homemade, handmade wavy flat noodles. They look glossy and delicious. When you eat them they have a bit of firmness, and these are solidly tasty too 😋

The toppings are soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), both jiggly and tender 😄　The seasoning is gentle and light, which felt different from the type at other shops where the flavor has thoroughly soaked in.
Rating (9.5/15): It's a shop particular about its ingredients, with "no chemical seasonings used" 😄　How about it for those who like healthy Okinawa soba?

When I ate here it was a super-hot lunchtime right after the rainy season had ended, but maybe because their concept is enjoying food naturally in an old house, the shop's windows were wide open with only electric fans, and no air conditioning was on (^_^;)　Everyone was eating while sweating, which in a sense was healthy too 😁

宜野湾そば.name: Ginowan Soba
宜野湾そば.desc: A famous shop also introduced in Horiemon's email newsletter. A customizable style with 3 kinds of noodles × 2 kinds of soup; the Gorogoro Soba loaded with chopped meat and the salt soft-bone pork rib soba are popular. Its sister shop is Churuge Soba in Uruma City.
t: ― 2nd visit (November 2023) ―
I ate here in November 2023. This shop is a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (Oct 1, 2023 – Feb 29, 2024)," and I went as my 17th of 34 shops 😊
Ginowan Soba (it's on the way toward the University of the Ryukyus from the Ganeko intersection on National Route 330)
I learned about this soba shop from Horiemon's email newsletter and ate here before, and this is my second time in a while 😁
Celebrity autographs displayed inside the shop
Lots of celebrity autographs are displayed inside. It's a famous shop loved by the locals 😊
Inside the shop

Last time there were customers, so I couldn't take photos of the inside, but this time it was past lunchtime and no one was there, so I took some photos. The parking lot fits several cars, and the inside is spacious too.
You can choose from 3 kinds of noodles and 2 kinds of soup.

This time I had decided to order the "Gorogoro Soba" introduced in the stamp rally booklet, and I chose the "light" soup. When I asked the staff about the noodles, they recommended the "wavy noodles," so I ordered it with "wavy noodles."

However, when I checked my previous blog after eating, I'd been recommended the same thing by the staff that time too and chosen "light soup" with "wavy noodles," so I thought I should have ordered something different this time (;^ω^)
Gorogoro soba　¥800 (light soup, wavy noodles)

Partly because there were no other customers, it came out quickly after I ordered. When it's this fast, you can grab a meal easily, which is nice. When I went to taste the soup first, I thought the soup's color was dark and it looked strong-flavored as I took a sip.
Sure enough, it's the "light" type as I ordered, but it still has a solid flavor and is delicious 😋

As for this soup, this time the wall inside said "Prepared in three stages with prefecture-raised chicken and pork. The classic light soup," so it seems to be a chicken and pork broth soup, but the menu in my previous blog said "bonito flakes, combined with the saltiness of soy sauce and seasonings," so maybe the broth base changed?
Gorogoro soba (medium)　¥800 (light soup, wavy noodles)

The wavy noodles have just the right firmness too; solidly tasty 😋　The meat in the toppings (braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), lean meat?) is chopped into small pieces, and though it was a medium size, it had quite a lot of volume.
Rating (9/15): Solidly tasty. I thought it was a fair bit higher level than when I ate here before. This is also a shop loved by the locals, so how about it when you're nearby.
― 1st visit (September 2021) ―
I ate here in September 2021. I learned about this place because it was introduced in Horiemon's email newsletter 😄
Ginowan Soba (it's on the way toward the University of the Ryukyus from the Ganeko intersection on National Route 330)
Menu

Horiemon had eaten the "Salt Soft-Bone Soki Soba" in his email newsletter, so I ordered the same item. It's the type where you can choose the soup and noodles, and this time I went with the "light bonito soup" and "wavy noodles" the staff recommended 😄
Salt soft-bone soki soba (large)　¥1,000
The soup clings well to the smooth wavy noodles; delicious 😋　There were lots of pork spare ribs (soki) too, and I got full.

Rating (9/15): It's solidly tasty, but since it was recommended by the gourmet Horiemon, my expectations were too high and I set the bar too high ^^;　I felt it didn't have the impact of my provisional #1 recommendation, EIBUN. However, this is also a shop loved by the locals, so how about it when you're nearby.

宮古そば ひらら.name: Miyako Soba Hirara
宮古そば ひらら.desc: An unusual Miyako soba shop inside a golf driving range. Its selling point is the traditional-style, un-Instagrammable "Soba" with the toppings hidden under the noodles. A blended broth of pork bone and bonito, with the pork bone coming through strongly.
t: I ate here in May 2024 😁 I learned about this shop because it was introduced in a local newspaper 😁　But this road is one I often take to the surf point I go to every weekend (Suicide Cliff Point) (^0^;)
I had absolutely no idea there was an Okinawa soba shop at a golf driving range (^0^;)
The "Miyako Soba Hirara" sign (the sign at the access road to the golf driving range along Prefectural Route 7)
The other side of the "Miyako Soba Hirara" sign. It's inside the golf driving range.
"Miyako Soba Hirara" is there when you head down the golf driving range access road.
Miyako Soba Hirara (it's inside the golf driving range)
Menu
From the menu, I somewhat randomly ordered the "Nankotsu Soba (regular)."
However, after I finished eating, I looked back at the newspaper article again and regretted it (^0^;)
It seems this shop's selling point was the "Soba" listed at the top of the menu.
Traditional Miyako soba is apparently characterized by the toppings being hidden at the bottom under the noodles, and the "Soba" at the top of the menu seems to be that.
At a glance it looks like just green onions and noodles; it makes "not Instagrammable" its selling point and seems to stick firmly to the old-fashioned traditional Miyako soba style.
This is my first Miyako soba since "Miyako Soba Ai" in Okinawa City, which I visited during the stamp rally, but Ai didn't have that style.
Since it just said "Soba," I mistakenly assumed it was simply plain soba (no toppings) (^0^;)　I should have ordered the "Soba."
Inside the shop (it's beside the golf driving range)
Inside the shop (it's beside the golf driving range)
Nankotsu soba (regular)　¥780
This one has the toppings sitting on top of the noodles as usual (^0^;)
The soup is a blended broth of pork bone and bonito, with the pork bone coming through.
It's solidly tasty.
Nankotsu soba (regular)　¥780
Next, the noodles. Medium-thin, roundish, and straight. A soft type. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are meltingly tender too, but there are spots where some sinewy texture remains.

Rating (9/15): Solidly tasty. I recommend the un-Instagrammable "Soba" with the toppings hidden under the noodles, which seems to be traditional for Miyako soba 😄　If you play golf, how about this driving range?

宮古そば愛.name: Miyako Soba Ai
宮古そば愛.desc: A night-owl Miyako soba shop open from 6 p.m. to 5 a.m. in the Nakanomachi nightlife district. A reassuring flavor with solid bonito broth, perfect for filling up before drinking or for finishing the night. It's nice that it accepts PayPay too.
t: I ate here in October 2023. This shop is a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (Oct 1, 2023 – Feb 29, 2024)," and I went as my 9th of 34 shops 😊
Miyako Soba Ai　It's got great character 😁

This shop's business hours are 18:00–5:00, so it's open at night 🤗　It's in an area of Okinawa City with lots of bars called "Nakanomachi," so it's an Okinawa soba shop for filling up before drinking or for finishing off the night after drinking (lol)
The nightlife district (Nakanomachi) where Miyako Soba Ai is. Since it was the weekend, there were lots of touts out on the street lol
Miyako soba (small) ¥750

Since it was nighttime, this time I ordered a smaller Okinawa soba, the "Miyako Soba (small)." There was a meal ticket machine, but it also supports cashless payment, and I was able to pay with PayPay. It's nice to be able to pay quickly 😁
First, a sip of the soup. The bonito broth base comes through solidly, a reassuring flavor 😊　Solidly tasty.
Miyako soba (small) ¥750
Next, the noodles. The noodles are a thin straight type. These also have a reassuring flavor. You can't go wrong lol

Near the downtown area where this shop is (Nakanomachi (Koza)) is the road to the US military base (Kadena Air Base) (commonly known as Gate Street or Airport Road), and nearby is the street that used to bustle with American servicemen as customers.
When I walked along this road for the first time in a while, hip-hop music was blasting from bars catering to foreigners, and the street felt like a club 🤗　It makes you want to dance (lol)

Rating (9/15): The soup has solid bonito broth and a can't-go-wrong, reassuring flavor. How about it at least once to finish off a night of drinking in Koza (Nakanomachi), Okinawa City 😁　If you head out to Gate Street, you can enjoy an atmosphere like being abroad too.
